questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm extended. This rule applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway:

options.text: The driver should honk their horn.
The driver should pass the animal as closely as possible.
The driver should be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no oncoming traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn drivers of dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no traffic from either direction may cross the center line to pass.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its lights flashing. You must:

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you do not drive next to the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you do not drive next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes if you can. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible.

questions.question: It is unlawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Motorcyclists need the full lane width to ride safely and maneuver.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a road is joining from the right side ahead.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use your brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas. Do not brake hard right away. Gradually slow down and gently apply the brakes as you pull off the road.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
Road conditions are not ideal for driving.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions are not ideal for driving.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They show that work is being done on or near the road. Drive with extra care when you see these signs.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beams.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.
questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Speed affects how far your vehicle travels before it stops. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop. Stay far behind the car in front of you at high speeds.

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When you approach a roundabout, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach a roundabout. Roundabouts are meant to be driven at low speeds. You may not need to stop if no cars or pedestrians are in the roundabout.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Running the engine while sitting in the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Every time you brake hard, your car uses fuel to speed back up. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid braking, you will use less gas.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bigger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that the driver cannot see in the mirrors.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow X on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to turn to a red X.
The signal is about to turn to a green arrow.
You can only use this lane to turn left.
You can drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only use this lane to turn left.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed throughout the day. A flashing yellow X means you can only use that lane to turn left.

questions.question: Before backing up your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Look behind your vehicle before you get in.
Only look to the sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look behind your vehicle before you get in.
questions.explanation: Look behind your vehicle before you get in. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians when you drive through intersections or turn.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to light up the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, slow down and drive carefully. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better in fog.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move as far right as possible before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes of traffic.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What do yellow-green signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Yellow-green signs warn about pedestrians, bicycles, and schools. Drive carefully in these areas.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the road onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Slow down without braking hard. Carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for traffic as you return to the road.

questions.question: You are on a divided multilane highway and see an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down and move out of the way. Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and stay a safe distance behind other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and stay a safe distance behind other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react without emergency braking. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into you.

questions.question: When parallel parking, how far from the curb should your car be?
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches
questions.explanation: Park no more than 12 inches from the curb. Park where drivers from both directions can see your car.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two one-way lanes with a median. Stay to the right.
